evidence: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:108-117 runs CountDevices in its own session, then the INSERT ... ON CONFLICT at database.go:120-153 runs in a separate WithDbSession. There is no transaction or lock. N concurrent new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, which overshoots the limit. The per-instance localCache (impl.go tagDeviceUI) does not dedupe across different device IDs or HA instances. The race is real but the overshoot is bounded by concurrency, so for a soft licensing-style cap this is low severity.

database.go:18 defines ErrDeviceLimitReached as a plain fmt.Errorf sentinel. client.go returns it from Authenticate, and authnimpl/service.go:190-222 joins it into authErr and returns it raw. The text is an internal error string, not a message shown to users. The real gap is that it is not an errutil error with a public message and status (unlike errCantAuthenticateReq = errutil.Unauthorized at service.go:46), so the HTTP layer gives a generic failure. Rewording the string alone would not help users.

packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:97 `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` has no annotation. With "strict": true (tsconfig.json:8) the property is inferred as type `undefined`, not `number | undefined` (packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200). Consumers of GrafanaBootConfig would not be able to treat it as a number. The same file already shows the fix at line 85: `loginError: string | undefined = undefined;`. The fix is a type annotation, not a different initial value.

client.go Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously with the request ctx instead of a goroutine with a 2-minute timeout. This is required to reject requests when the limit is reached. DB errors other than ErrDeviceLimitReached are only logged (client.go: a.log.Warn), so they do not fail authentication. That part of the claim is overstated. Latency is real: a slow DB now blocks the request, and the extra CountDevices query (database.go:110) runs whenever device_limit > 0. This is mitigated by the 29-minute localCache in impl.go tagDeviceUI. The change is an intentional tradeoff.

database_test.go TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a second, new device ID gets ErrDeviceLimitReached. It never calls CreateOrUpdateDevice again for the original device "32mdo31deeqwes" once the limit is reached. That is the updateDevice path at database.go:72-103, which this feature depends on so existing users are not locked out.

pkg/setting/setting.go:1654 reads [auth.anonymous] device_limit, but grep finds no device_limit in conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini or docs/. Grafana documents every setting in defaults.ini/sample.ini and in the configure-grafana docs. Users cannot find the option or learn that 0 means unlimited and that new devices are rejected (with existing ones updated) once the limit is reached.

database.go:72-103: updateDevice is only reached when count >= limit (database.go:114-116). Both scenarios the reviewer lists are correctly 'limit reached'. A device that does not exist would be a new device. A device outside the 30-day window is not counted as active, so reactivating it would also exceed the limit. MySQL's 'unchanged row gives 0 affected rows' case does not apply: Grafana connects with clientFoundRows=true (pkg/services/sqlstore/sqlstore.go:287), so matched rows are counted.

The duplication is real, but the reviewer has the location slightly wrong. anonymousDeviceExpiration = 30*24h is defined in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:16 and api/api.go:18, not impl.go:18. impl.go:25 also keeps the same value as thirtyDays (used at impl.go:70). That makes three copies of the 30-day window, which store, API and usage stats must keep in sync. Exporting it from anonstore and reusing it would remove the drift risk.

setting.go:1654 uses MustInt64(0), and database.go:108 only enforces the limit when s.deviceLimit > 0. A negative value therefore acts exactly like 0 (unlimited) and cannot cause wrong behavior. Grafana does not usually validate other numeric ini values like this, so adding validation is optional at most.
